daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Rolling Average Momentum
daily_quests.description: Using the ASX 200 historical prices dataset, calculate a 20-day rolling average for the top 5 most volatile stocks (by standard deviation of daily returns). Use window functions to compute the rolling average and rank stocks by volatility. Return: stock symbol, date, closing price, 20-day rolling average, volatility rank, and row number partitioned by stock ordered by date. Filter results to show only the last 10 trading days for each stock.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning & Aggregation
daily_quests.description: Download NSW Road Crash Data and perform the following: (1) Clean missing values in crash severity, accident type, and location columns using appropriate strategies (mode for categorical, forward-fill for temporal). (2) Create a new column 'crash_cluster' grouping crashes into geographic regions using postcode ranges. (3) Generate a summary CSV with columns: region, total_crashes, fatalities, serious_injuries, most_common_accident_type, and average_vehicles_involved. (4) Validate data integrity by asserting no nulls remain in critical columns.

daily_quests.title: Australian Weather Anomalies Pipeline
daily_quests.description: Build a data pipeline combining Python and SQL: (1) In Python, download Bureau of Meteorology weather observations (or use Kaggle Australian Weather dataset), clean temperature and rainfall columns, and load into a local SQLite database. (2) In SQL, use CTEs and window functions to identify temperature anomalies: calculate the 30-year normal (average) temperature for each month and location, then flag days where actual temperature deviates >2 standard deviations from the norm. (3) Export results showing: station_id, date, observed_temp, normal_temp, deviation_std, is_anomaly. (4) Create a Python summary script that reads the SQL output and generates a report of the top 10 most anomalous days across all stations.
daily_quests.dataset: Australian Weather observations — Bureau of Meteorology / Kaggle
